title: Who-does-what card with the guest list written as a limit, not a hope
body:
A one-page card that a programme lead can hand to four people on day one, with the guest's limits written down rather than assumed.

What I will deliver, in the attachment, as one printable page: four roles (programme lead, instructor, learner, guest recruiter), each with three things they do and two they do not. The guest recruiter's card is limited to demo day: they see the demo and the pitches, they do not get the class history or the files, and they are removed after the session — that is the point the brief makes and I will make it explicit.

Every action will be checked against what zedu.chat actually names: channels and announcements for the lead, file sharing and assignment discussions for the instructor, threads and direct messages for the learner. Anything not stated on the public site — who can remove a guest, whether a guest can post in a channel — goes in a marked "needs confirmation" list instead of the card.

Fictional bootcamp throughout, no Telex, no Enterprise pricing, no per-student fees, and no line that suggests AI replaces an instructor; the AI line will say it summarises and answers questions, which is what the About page says.

Time: same day. Reviewer check: pick any action on the card and find where zedu.chat names it, or find it on the needs-confirmation list.
